newsitem.title: CANADA: Fire reported in Toronto subway station.
newsitem.headline: Fire reported in Toronto subway station.

text.p: Between 60 and 100 people were evacuated from a Toronto subway station on Wednesday night after a fire sent smoke billowing through the building and adjoining subway tunnels, police said.

Toronto police said no one was seriously injured in the fire, which began at about 7.30 p.m. EDT (2330 GMT) in the Danforth and Donlands station, but several people appeared to have been overcome by smoke.

Police said it was not clear whether the smoke was coming from a fire in a subway train or tunnel. Service on the subway line was suspended as police, fire and rescue crews responded to the fire alarm.

The Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) said all passengers and subway personnel had left the station, and about 40 people were taken to hospital to be treated for minor smoke inhalation. The eastern portion of the subway system was closed.
Transit officials said it appeared that the fire broke out in a pile of track ties stored in a train marshalling yard near the station and that smoke was drawn down into the subway tunnels.
Smoke could be seen billowing from subway tunnel vents. Streets providing access to the Donlands station and others nearby were closed off to all traffic except for emergency vehicles.
